memory_candidates.content: Editing an indexed context/docs markdown file in this repo (one listed in an extension's index-entries.json) requires its line_count entry to stay in sync or doc-lint (gate 3) fails. Fix with: REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write (must run with REPO_ROOT set when invoked from the source store, not the deployed copy). If the same index-entries.json file already carries other sibling tasks' unrelated uncommitted line_count corrections (common in a multi-task /orchestrate batch), fix your own entry's content in the working tree (satisfies gate verification, which reads the working tree directly) but do not commit the whole file via git-commit-scoped.sh -- it stages a whole named path with no sub-file hunk granularity, so committing would over-stage the unrelated hunks into your task's history. Leave the file dirty for a later commit to pick up, and use `git restore --staged -- <path>` to undo any exploratory `git apply --cached` staging rather than leaving a stray partial stage.

A plan/report's cited file/line or script-name claim (a 'carried figure') can go stale within the same /orchestrate batch if a concurrently or previously dispatched sibling task lands a same-day commit touching that exact call site. Before writing a claim into a documentation deliverable, re-grep the live source for the cited symbol/script rather than trusting the plan's citation verbatim -- e.g. orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's memory-context call site was swapped from memory-retrieve.sh to sapience-retrieve.sh by a same-day prior commit, after the plan and report for this task had already cited the old name.
